sources_legend: Official list: the PlayStation 5 trophy list for Grand Theft Auto VI as published by PlayStation and mirrored identically by Exophase and PSNProfiles (names, descriptions, grades). Points: PlayStation's standard trophy values. Method notes cite the series' own conventions (GTA V's 100% checklist and stunt/race design, RDR2's stranger-strand structure) as named sources; no text is copied from any guide.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: What: the platinum, awarded the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned. How: there is nothing separate to do — work the six roadmap stages in order, keep the missable watch list clear before the endgame, and let the 100% gold (A Long Road) be your final grind. When it can be missed: never directly, but a missed watch-list trophy on a single save can force a second playthrough, so export your tracker progress before the final missions. Tip: the tracker counts this one automatically when 54 of 54 are ticked.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); PlayStation platinum rules.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: What: finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission. How: start a new game and play the prologue through to its end card — the trophy pops on completion, no score or medal is required. The mission doubles as the movement, driving and combat tutorial, so take the prompts slowly if this is your first hour. When it can be missed: it cannot; it is the first thing the game asks you to do. Tip: every later earn-rate snapshot shows this at effectively 100% of players — if it has not popped, your save has not finished the prologue.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: What: finish Chapter 1 of the story. How: follow the chapter's mission markers in order; the trophy lands on the chapter-complete screen. Chapter 1 introduces the second protagonist and the partner-switch, which several later trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) build on. When it can be missed: story progress cannot be skipped or locked out. Tip: start the cheap open-world habits now — discovering vehicles (Whip It Good) and registering them in the Scooter Bros app (On the Spot) is painless while the map is new.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: What: finish Chapter 2. How: play the chapter's missions through; the name is printed with asterisks on PlayStation itself, so search for it exactly as shown. Chapter 2 opens the drug-running economy that Dime on the Dollar ($250,000 of laundered Marked Bills) later measures — bank marked bills with your contacts from here on instead of spending them. When it can be missed: it cannot. Tip: keep one save at the chapter break; chapter-gated strand missions (the Watch list) are easiest to sweep right after a chapter ends.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: What: finish Chapter 3. How: complete the chapter's mission chain; the trophy pops at the chapter card. By this point both protagonists' safehouses and the full Vice City district set are open, which unlocks most activity types for Master of None. When it can be missed: it cannot. Tip: mid-story is the cheapest time to clear the activity sampler (Master of None) and the first collectible-card sets, while mission variety is still carrying you across the map.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: What: finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the finale arc. How: play through the chapter missions; completion is all that is asked. Treat the chapter-complete save as your point-of-no-return backup: several Watch-list items (strand finales, partner feats, story-beat moments) are far easier before the endgame sequence starts. When it can be missed: the chapter itself cannot, but what you leave unswept gets harder after it. Tip: export your tracker file here and name it — if a finale choice locks anything, you have a clean way back.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: What: finish the final story mission — one of only two golds on the list. How: the finale unlocks after Chapter 4 and the named missions are done; complete it at any difficulty and with any ending the game offers, the trophy is for completion, not for a choice. Before you start it, clear the missable watch list (especially Actions Speak Louder, which is decided by choices) and finish the stranger strands. When it can be missed: the mission cannot, but choice-based trophies resolve here. Tip: after the credits, free roam continues — everything not choice-gated can still be swept toward A Long Road.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: What: complete the story mission Breakfast Run. How: it sits inside Chapter 1's chain — play the missions in marker order and it arrives early; finish it to the end card. When it can be missed: named story missions cannot be skipped; if you are past Chapter 1 without it, check the mission list, because it means a chain step is still open. Tip: mission-replay (once unlocked) also completes any named-mission trophy you somehow passed in a co-op session, per the series' usual rules.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: What: complete The Cartel Heist, a named story mission. How: it is a set-piece heist inside the chapter flow — bring armour, a fast getaway car staged before the final objective, and both protagonists' abilities charged. Completion is the only condition; take the loud or quiet approach the mission offers as you prefer. When it can be missed: it cannot. Tip: this heist is the rehearsal for Maximum Withdrawal (5 bank vaults) — the vault-and-escape rhythm you learn here is the one the open-world robberies reuse.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: What: complete the story mission Child's Play. How: follow the story chain; the mission is a character beat rather than a combat test, so just play it to the end card. When it can be missed: it cannot. Tip: story-beat missions like this one are where the one-off moment trophies hide (a cocktail, a bowling follow-through) — if a prompt to interact appears during a quiet scene, take it before moving on.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: What: complete the story mission Headliners. How: play the mission chain in order; finish Headliners to its end card. When it can be missed: it cannot. Tip: if a named mission seems missing from your log, its prerequisite is usually an unfinished stranger strand or a phone call — sleep at a safehouse to advance the clock and re-check the map.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: What: complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at Vice City International Airport. How: finish the mission as scripted. This is also the mission window the Catch Me If You Can trophy hangs off — an unscheduled departure at VCIA — so before you close the mission out, look for the chance to leave the airport in a way the plan did not schedule (an aircraft, a service vehicle) if you want both in one pass. When it can be missed: the mission cannot; its side trophy can. Tip: make a manual save at the mission start.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: What: complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. How: a late-chapter set piece — stock up beforehand, use Combat Focus for crowded rooms (five takedowns in one use is the Gunslinger trophy, and this mission's densities are a natural place to try it). When it can be missed: it cannot. Tip: named-mission trophies are the spine of stages 1–2; if your tracker shows one open after the finale, mission replay is the way back.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: What: reach 100% on the game's own completion counter — the second gold and the platinum's real gate. How: GTA's 100% is a checklist, not literally everything: story complete, stranger strands done, the activity and collectible quotas the in-game stats page names (stunts, races, cards, spots), properties owned and the miscellaneous feats. Work from the in-game 100% screen, not from vibes: it itemises what is left. When it can be missed: the counter cannot be locked, but choice-gated trophies still need their own save discipline. Tip: leave this open in the tracker until the stats page itself reads 100% — several silvers (Cunning Stunts, Don't Touch My Deck) are subsets of it, so they fall first.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V 100%-checklist conventions (the series' in-game completion screen).

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: What: complete 250 stunt jumps/events across Leonida. How: stunts are the marked ramps, jumps and stunt locations scattered over the map; a stunt counts when you land it cleanly. Route them by district while doing other sweeps — the tracker on the in-game stats page holds the running count. Method that works in every GTA: a fast bike shortens most run-ups, and a failed attempt can be retried on the spot. When it can be missed: never; the world stays open. Tip: do stunts in daylight — landing zones are much easier to read, and 250 is a marathon, not a session.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V stunt-jump conventions.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: What: sample every activity type once — races, drone races, shooting range, fishing, arcade, meditation, hunting and the rest of the map's activity icons. How: you do not need to win or finish most of them; starting (and where the game asks, completing a first round) registers the type. Sweep it mid-story when the whole map is open: one icon of each colour, an hour at most. When it can be missed: never. Tip: this is the cheapest scouting run for the grind trophies — note which activity types you enjoy, because you will be doing 250 stunts and 20 race wins later.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: What: gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge (PlayStation tracks the challenge count — 42 in the published list data). How: ranges sit at gun stores and facilities across Leonida; each challenge is a scored course with a gold threshold. Learn one course's target order, then chase golds course by course; accuracy beats speed until the medal maths says otherwise. When it can be missed: never; challenges are replayable. Tip: finish story combat upgrades first — Combat Focus control and fuller weapon handling make the later courses markedly easier.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: What: win the Top Fun drone race at every location that hosts one. How: a win, not a medal — first place at each site. Drone courses reward memorised lines over raw speed: run each course once to learn the gate order, then race it. When it can be missed: never; races are repeatable. Tip: these wins are separate from the 20 race wins of Earn Cash, Not Kudos, so do not expect the counters to share — track them apart in the checklist.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: What: win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. How: Leonida's race series span street, off-road, water and air; a win in each unique event counts once. Start with the short point-to-points near Vice City and work outward; bring the fastest owned vehicle each class allows. When it can be missed: never. Tip: if a class keeps beating you, its later events are usually easier than its opener — hop around the map instead of grinding one start line.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: What: beat Cal, the fishing rival, in his fishing challenge. How: fishing opens at the coast and keys; the challenge is a head-to-head catch contest. Learn the cast-and-reel timing on ordinary fish first, use the best rod and bait you can buy, and target the heavier species the challenge scores. When it can be missed: never; Cal will fish again tomorrow. Tip: it is fitting that the game's first mission is called Gone Fishing — the fishing system is a headline feature, so its upgrade path (better tackle at bait shops) is the intended difficulty lever.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: What: complete one arcade game, start to finish, at any arcade cabinet in Leonida. How: cabinets live in arcades, bars and diners; pick the shortest game on the machine's menu and play it to its end screen — quitting at the last level does not count. When it can be missed: never. Tip: one of the cheapest trophies on the list; grab it during the Master of None sampler so the arcade visit does double duty.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableNote: Strand finale — finish Andy's strand before the endgame to be safe.
trophies.guide: What: finish Andy's stranger strand — every mission in his chain, through its final one. How: strands open from a map marker and advance by phone calls and return visits; work each strand to its end rather than leaving finales for later. The strand system is the series' Strangers & Freaks design (RDR2's stranger missions work the same way): chains can look finished a mission before they are. When it can be missed: strand finales are the classic soft-lock risk in GTA design — complete them before the final story arc, which is why this sits on the watch list. Tip: after each strand mission, sleep once; the next step usually calls you.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 / GTA V stranger-strand conventions.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableNote: Strand finale — finish Kenton's strand before the endgame to be safe.
trophies.guide: What: finish Kenton's stranger strand through its final mission. How: follow his marker chain and calls to the end; his strand is water-flavoured (the title is a Jaws joke), so expect boat work — a decent boat of your own shortens the fetch legs. When it can be missed: same strand rule as Andy — finales before the endgame. Tip: strands share the Strangers & Freaks silver counter (8 strands), so each finale is doing double duty.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 / GTA V stranger-strand conventions.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableNote: Strand finale — finish Billy's strand before the endgame to be safe.
trophies.guide: What: finish Billy's stranger strand through its final mission. How: work his chain from its first marker; a rider's strand means long road legs, so a fast bike in a nearby garage is the practical tool. When it can be missed: strand rule — finales before the endgame. Tip: if Billy's next step does not appear, strands often gate on time of day; wait at a safehouse and check the map at dawn and dusk.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 / GTA V stranger-strand conventions.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: Needs 8 full strands — start strands early so finales are not rushed at the end.
trophies.guide: What: complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida — a silver, and the umbrella over the named strand trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone are five of them). How: a strand counts when its final mission is done, not when it is started. There are more strands than the five named trophies, so pick up every question-mark marker you pass. When it can be missed: strands themselves stay on the map, but finales belong before the endgame — the watch flag is about pacing, not a hard lock. Tip: the tracker groups all six stranger trophies in stage 3; clear the stage as a block.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V Strangers & Freaks conventions.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableNote: Strand finale — finish Randy's strand before the endgame to be safe.
trophies.guide: What: finish Randy's stranger strand through its final mission. How: a supply-running chain — expect delivery legs under time or heat pressure; stage a clean, fast vehicle before accepting each step and the finales stop being stressful. When it can be missed: strand rule — finales before the endgame. Tip: Randy's deliveries overlap the marked-bill economy; launder what his runs pay you toward Dime on the Dollar.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 / GTA V stranger-strand conventions.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableNote: Strand finale — finish Tyrone's strand before the endgame to be safe.
trophies.guide: What: finish Tyrone's stranger strand through its final mission. How: follow his chain to the end; keep both protagonists available, since strand finales sometimes script a switch. When it can be missed: strand rule — finales before the endgame. Tip: with Tyrone done, count your strands: five named finales plus any three others completes the Strangers & Freaks silver.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 / GTA V stranger-strand conventions.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: What: meditate at every meditation spot in the state. How: spots are quiet, scenic points — rooftops, piers, hilltops — marked by a small prompt when you stand on them. This is a fixed collectible set: the count is finite and the in-game stats track it. Sweep district by district alongside stunt jumps, which share the same rooftops and ridges. When it can be missed: never. Tip: sunrise and sunset visits are not just prettier — the spots are easier to spot when their marker catches low light.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: What: hunt the unique animal Bret sends you after. How: take Bret's hunt from his marker or call, track the animal in its named habitat, and make the kill clean — unique-animal hunts in the series' design (RDR2's legendary animals) are one-spawn creatures with a fixed territory, so search the territory, not the whole map. When it can be missed: the hunt stays available; a spooked animal returns after you leave and come back. Tip: go at dawn with a scoped rifle and full Combat Focus; unique animals are usually placed off-road, so bring an off-roader.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 legendary-hunt conventions.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: What: complete any 3 full Collectible Card sets. How: cards are found in the world and grouped into themed sets (the deck UI shows each set's members and where its theme lives — casinos, boardwalks, bars). Finish the three smallest sets first; the deck screen's per-set counts tell you which those are. When it can be missed: never; cards are permanent pickups. Tip: cards cluster where their theme lives, so a set sweep doubles as exploration credit for The Goodtime State.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); RDR2 cigarette-card set conventions.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: What: perform the WAiNK interaction at 100 different locations. How: WAiNK spots are marked photo-style points of interest across Leonida — landmarks, signs, vistas. Each unique location counts once; the stats page tracks the total. Treat it as the sightseeing set: route it with meditation spots and stunts, and it finishes almost by itself over a full playthrough. When it can be missed: never. Tip: if a spot will not trigger, stand in the marker's centre and face the landmark it names — the prompt is positional.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: What: complete 50 challenges from the game's challenge board. How: challenges are the short scored tasks the world offers — range courses, race events, stunt scores, delivery times. Fifty sounds like a lot until you notice most activity trophies are made of challenges: the shooting-range golds, races and stunts all feed this counter. When it can be missed: never. Tip: check the counter before grinding anything new — most players find this pops during stage 4 without a dedicated session.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableNote: Needs a partner session — easiest while story missions keep both protagonists together.
trophies.guide: What: with your partner (the other protagonist) alongside, earn a 4-star Wanted Level and lose it completely. How: the reliable recipe — commit crimes together in free roam until four stars, then break line of sight and hide (alleys, water, a vehicle swap) until the stars drain. Both characters must be present for the escape, so do it when the story has them paired, or in partner free-roam. When it can be missed: not locked, but the paired windows are guaranteed during story chapters — the watch flag is a reminder to bank it early. Tip: a Pay 'n Spray-style respray or a tunnel run shortens the drain; do not re-offend while stars are flashing.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableNote: Needs a partner session and one continuous Wanted Level across 3 robberies.
trophies.guide: What: rob 3 shops in a row with your partner while one Wanted Level stays alive the whole time. How: pick a district with three shops close together (a strip-mall row is ideal), rob the first, and drive — do not hide — between shops so the stars never fully drain; the third till completes it. Keep the car repaired and fuelled before you start. When it can be missed: not locked, but it needs the paired-protagonist setup, so bank it during a story chapter that keeps them together. Tip: rob shops whose doors face the street — seconds spent parking are seconds the Wanted Level spends draining.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: What: discover 100 different vehicles — entering a vehicle model for the first time registers it. How: traffic variety is district-based: ports have trucks and forklifts, the keys have boats' land cousins, rich districts have the exotics. Steal promiscuously early: every new model you sit in counts, and the compendium-style vehicle list shows what you have. When it can be missed: never. Tip: airports, marinas and construction sites are the densest sources of odd models — one pass through each is worth twenty street cars.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: What: kill 5 enemies during one activation of Combat Focus (the slow-motion aiming ability). How: you need a crowd and a full ability meter: gang operations (Pest Control) and the Operation Savage Glory set piece pack rooms densely enough. Activate when at least five enemies are in one sightline, use a high-capacity weapon, and prioritise headshots to stretch the meter. When it can be missed: never — attempts are unlimited. Tip: upgrade the ability first if the meter drains too fast; five takedowns is tuned for a mid-story meter, not the tutorial one.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: Tied to the VCIA mission window — take the unscheduled way out while you are at the airport.
trophies.guide: What: leave VCIA (Vice City International Airport) in a way no plan scheduled — steal an aircraft or vehicle and depart during the airport sequence. How: the natural window is the VCIA Takedown mission (Hi-Jacked): before finishing its final objective, take an unscheduled exit — a plane on the apron is the cleanest read of the description. Mission replay is the fallback if your first pass missed it. When it can be missed: this is one of the list's genuinely missable feats, because it hangs off a scripted location visit; it is flagged likely-missable straight from the description's wording. Tip: save manually at the airport before the finale of the mission, and try departures until it pops.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: What: the Rhino is GTA's tank, and the description is a joke about the heat inside one — the feat is a tank rampage milestone (survive the military response a Rhino attracts). How: steal a Rhino from the military presence or a base incursion, then stay in it while the Wanted Level and the army's answer build; the trophy pops as the situation peaks. When it can be missed: never; Rhinos can be stolen again. Tip: keep moving — a stationary Rhino is a target for every rocket in Leonida; bridges and tunnels reset the worst of the response.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA series Rhino conventions.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: What: rob a jewelry store and get away with no detection — no alarm state, no Wanted Level earned from the robbery itself. How: case the store first (cameras, guard posts), go in quiet — suppressed approach, no shots, smash-and-grab the cases and out the back before the silent alarm's timer matters. The series' jewelry heist (GTA V's first score) is the template: speed and silence, not firepower. When it can be missed: never; stores can be robbed again after a cooldown. Tip: park the getaway car at the rear exit with the engine running and the door open.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V jewelry-heist conventions.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: What: rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — a silver, and the open-world sequel to the story's Cartel Heist. How: bank branches with vaults are marked once scouted; each robbery is breach, vault, escape. Vary your banks — five different vaults is the safe reading of the description — and upgrade your approach as the heat scales: later vaults answer faster. When it can be missed: never; banks reset. Tip: escape is the hard half: pre-stage a fast car two streets away and swap into it once the first stars land, the same rhythm as Break the Bank.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: What: rob one armored money truck and escape with the take. How: armored trucks run routes in free roam — the classic blitz is to block the truck, breach the rear doors (explosives or sustained fire on the locks), grab the cash and break line of sight fast; the name is a nod to GTA V's Blitz Play heist, which used the same truck. When it can be missed: never; trucks keep circulating. Tip: do it near a tunnel or parking structure — the escape, not the breach, is where these go wrong.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V Blitz Play conventions.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: What: uncover the whole map — every district of the state of Leonida visited. How: the map fog clears where you travel; the last percentages are always the same places: the far keys, the swamp interior, the small islands and the mountain roads. A plane or helicopter pass at altitude clears coastal and island fog quickly, then mop up inland gaps on the ground. When it can be missed: never. Tip: leave this until stage 4's sweeps are done — stunts, spots and cards will clear most of the map for you, and what remains will be obvious.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: What: rob an illegal operation owned by each of Leonida's gangs — one per gang, not the same gang repeatedly. How: gang operations (labs, fronts, stash businesses) sit in gang territory; the map's gang shading or your contacts tell you whose is whose. Hit one of each, take the take, escape. When it can be missed: never; operations restock. Tip: these crowded interiors are also the best Gunslinger stages — five enemies in one Combat Focus is easier here than anywhere in free roam.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableNote: A quiet story-beat style moment — take the interaction when the game offers it.
trophies.guide: What: have the cocktail-with-a-view moment on Ocean Beach — a deliberate quiet beat, named like a postcard. How: the interaction is offered at Ocean Beach (the beachfront strip) — at a beach bar or during the story beat that puts you there with a drink in reach; accept the prompt and let the moment play out. When it can be missed: moments like this are usually repeatable at the location, but the scripted version is missable if you rush the scene — hence the watch flag. Tip: if the prompt never appears in free roam, it belongs to a story visit; mission replay restores it.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableNote: A set-piece exit during a story beat — drive out through the glass when you are in the showroom.
trophies.guide: What: escape a vehicle showroom by driving through its glass front — 'in classic style' is the series winking at GTA V's Franklin, who did exactly this in his first mission. How: during the showroom sequence, get in a car inside and drive out through the window instead of any door the game offers. When it can be missed: likely missable — it hangs on one scripted location visit; if the sequence ends another way, mission replay is the route back. Tip: any car on the showroom floor works; pick the one facing the glass.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V series-history reference in the description itself.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: What: complete the follow-through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — the title is GTA IV's most famous phone call, and the trophy is the alley's signature interaction. How: visit the alley (a Kolt & Associates office with its own lanes, in the game's joke), and do the bowling interaction through to its follow-through — a full game or the scripted throw the alley offers, depending on how the scene is built; either way, finish the interaction rather than walking out mid-way. When it can be missed: the alley stays open, so treat it as repeatable. Tip: bowling alleys in this series hide mini-game depth — if a score is asked, a straight, medium-power release down the middle is the reliable line.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA IV series-history reference in the title.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missableNote: A partner feat — bank it while the story keeps both protagonists paired.
trophies.guide: What: a partner milestone — the two-protagonist partnership reaching its 'mass appeal' moment, the pair's shared feat rather than a solo one. How: partner feats in this list resolve through shared play: keep both protagonists active together (shared free-roam feats, joint escapes, co-op mission completions all feed the partnership), and this pops as the pair's joint record peaks. When it can be missed: not hard-locked, but it belongs with the other partner trophies in stage 5 — do them as a block while paired play is guaranteed. Tip: if you are unsure what is counting, the stats page's partner section is the arbiter — check it before and after a paired session.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: Choice-gated by its own description — resolve your choices on a save you can return to.
trophies.guide: What: the choice trophy — its whole description is 'Choices made (for better or worse)', which means it is awarded for a decision (or the set of decisions) the story puts to you. How: when the game stops and asks — spare or punish, take or refuse, side with one partner or the other — the trophy hangs on one of those forks. Because the description does not say which fork, the safe method is the save discipline: keep a manual save before every obvious story fork from Chapter 3 onward, and if the credits roll without it, reload the fork saves and choose the other way. When it can be missed: likely missable by design — this is the list's clearest choice-gated trophy, flagged straight from its description. Tip: this is the strongest reason your stage-2 export of the tracker exists; forks are cheap to revisit with saves and expensive without them.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableNote: Reads as fail-then-succeed — if you ace everything first try, engineer the failure deliberately.
trophies.guide: What: 'Second time's the charm' — a fail-state trophy: fail at something the game tracks, then succeed at the same thing on the retry. How: the natural candidates are the scored activities (a race lost then won, a range course failed then passed) and mission retries. If it has not popped during honest play, do it deliberately: enter a short race, lose it on purpose, immediately re-enter and win. When it can be missed: not locked, but a flawless player can starve it — the watch flag exists for them. Tip: the cheapest deliberate fail is a 30-second race near a safehouse; the pair of attempts takes two minutes.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableNote: A hidden one-off event the description refuses to explain — treat strange encounters as once-only.
trophies.guide: What: the list's UFO-joke trophy — an X-Files title over a description that just asks 'What the hell just happened?', which in GTA language means a scripted weird encounter: the strange lights / abduction-style event the series hides for explorers. How: these events are found, not assigned — they trigger at a specific remote place at a specific time (the series' habit: a mountain, a swamp or the desert-equivalent at night, often weather-gated). When a strange encounter starts, stay in it until it resolves; leaving mid-event is how these are lost. When it can be missed: likely missable as a one-off scripted event, flagged from the description's own evasiveness. Tip: night exploration for The Goodtime State's last fog corners is when most players meet it — keep your phone camera ready in-game and do not fast-travel away from anything odd.
trophies.sources: Official PlayStation list (Exophase / PSNProfiles); GTA V UFO-encounter conventions.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: What: knock down a group of pedestrians with a melee drive-by — swing a melee weapon from a moving vehicle and 'bowl' the group. How: you need a tight group (a queue, a crosswalk crowd, a beach gathering), a bike or open car that allows melee swings, and one pass that connects with the group in a single swing arc. When it can be missed: never; crowds respawn. Tip: a motorcycle at moderate speed is the tool — too fast and the swing misses, too slow and it is just assault. Beach boardwalks at midday have the densest groups.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: What: launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. How: marked bills come from robberies and the drug economy (Chapter 2 opens it); they are not spendable until laundered, and your contacts take a cut — the counter is the amount laundered, not held. Make laundering a habit after every score rather than a stage-5 grind: bank the bills, run the contact, repeat. When it can be missed: never; the economy never closes. Tip: Randy's strand deliveries and gang-operation robberies are the richest marked-bill sources on the list — chain them.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: What: spend a cumulative $100,000 in shops — clothes, weapons, vehicles services, food, everything with a till. How: this is a playthrough-total counter, not a single spree; it lands naturally if you buy garages' worth of gear, and Little Boxes (all garage properties) alone moves it most of the way. When it can be missed: never. Tip: do not waste money chasing it early — heist payouts make it trivial by stage 5, and money spent is money the laundering counter could have used first.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: What: buy every garage property on the market. How: garages are purchasable properties scattered by district; the property section of the map lists what is for sale and its price. This is a money trophy wearing a property trophy's clothes — the total bill is the obstacle, so it belongs after the heists and the laundering economy are running. When it can be missed: never; properties stay listed. Tip: buy the cheap rural garages first — the count matters, not the prestige, and each garage is also vehicle storage for the 100-vehicle discovery sweep.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: What: register 10 vehicles as yours through the Scooter Bros app — the game's vehicle-ownership app. How: when you take a vehicle you want to keep, register it in the app (the prompt appears for eligible vehicles); ten registrations is the whole ask. Register variety, not ten copies of one car — the app is also how insured personal vehicles are managed. When it can be missed: never. Tip: start in Chapter 1 — every story-gifted car is a free registration, and ten arrives long before the 100-vehicle discovery trophy does.
